cases.purpose: Select all eligible outside-session PIDs while excluding the real caller, its session, kernel and malformed records.
cases.oracle: Guest-only parser, PID/mount namespace, seccomp and filesystem confinement controls run in setup. Each observation runs inside a separately controlled private PID/proc namespace containing only owned processes. Each guarded observation rechecks confinement, actual caller PID/SID and fixture. The none and unreadable cases first run a nonempty baseline in the same shell and fixture; unreadable then seals that root and confirms EACCES. Expected sets are independent of candidate output; race synchronizes deletion during stat read. The guarded caller starts a new session inside that namespace; guest controls require its visible positive SID to equal its PID and agree with getsid and proc stat.
cases.comparison: The independently reviewed primary must implement helpers/killall5-dry-run-reviewed-gate.json before using runner verdicts. The gate separates raw capture integrity from candidate output semantics, checks the per-invocation controls and exact unreadable-root diagnostic, and preserves reached product failures even if later infrastructure is incomplete.
cases.candidate_script:
outer=$(/usr/bin/readlink /proc/self/ns/pid) || exit 90
exec /usr/bin/unshare --user --map-user=2000 --map-group=2000 --mount --pid --fork --mount-proc /usr/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c 'if ! /usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/killall5-dry-run-reviewed.py namespace-check "$1" candidate >"$HOME/events.jsonl" 2>"$HOME/prepare.log"; then exit 90; fi
/usr/bin/setsid --wait ./guard "$2" --noprofile --norc -c "$3" &
pid=$!
rc=0
wait "$pid" || rc=$?
exit "$rc"
' namespace-init "$outer" "$BASH" 'printf '"'"'{"stage":"guard-enter","pid":%s}\n'"'"' "$$" >>"$HOME/events.jsonl"
if ! ulimit -f 128; then printf '"'"'{"stage":"ulimit-failed"}\n'"'"' >>"$HOME/events.jsonl"; exit 90; fi
printf '"'"'{"stage":"ulimit-ok"}\n'"'"' >>"$HOME/events.jsonl"

cases.purpose: Exclude the caller session and self when the guarded caller is a nonleader and its visible session leader remains alive.
cases.oracle: A separate guest setup control checks a live visible session leader and distinct nonleader in a private PID/proc namespace. The nonleader candidate runs under the existing signal and filesystem guards while its session-leader shell waits. Before its observation, independent getsid calls, both live proc stat records and PID namespace links establish positive SID = leader PID != caller PID. Synthetic self has an outside SID; separate same-session records carry the actual SID. The independent selected set contains all four eligible outside-session PIDs.
cases.comparison: The primary must independently implement and review the pinned gate. Require complete scope and PID/session preconditions and raw capture, then compare the entire PID set, stderr and status against the role oracle; selected same-session or self records are candidate failures. Missing or invalid nonleader context is incomplete infrastructure.
